source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Send command: ipmitool user list <Channel number>

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

historical_reviews.gpt_v2: FULLY AUTOMATABLE / CHANGED correctly requires supported-channel discovery, separate complete `user list <channel>` reads, protected credentials, untruncated raw output, slot/access/privilege normalization, redaction and a strict no-write boundary.

original_test_intent: Verify IPMI displays the complete current BMC user-slot inventory correctly for every Project-relevant management channel, including usernames, enable/access flags and channel privilege, without changing accounts or channel access.
original_method: Verify the BMC and ipmitool version; discover or receive the supported management channel set; query `ipmitool user list <channel>` separately for each relevant channel using protected credentials; preserve complete raw redacted output; normalize slot ID, name, Call-in, Link Auth, IPMI Msg, privilege and empty/disabled state; classify auth/transport errors separately; optionally cross-check read-only UI/API state; prove no write occurred.
manual_activity: An owner supplies/approves channel and field semantics, expected baseline and redaction. Once those inputs and protected access exist, the inventory is automatable and needs no physical action or write approval. A human reviews the resulting matrix and owns the verdict.
required_inputs: Supported management channels and discovery semantics
User-list field, privilege and empty/disabled meanings
Protected credential mechanism and approved cipher/TLS-equivalent policy
Expected account/slot baseline or read-only comparison source
Reviewed revision/scope if the referenced internal Script is used
safety_requirements: Do not place BMC passwords in `-P`, URLs, history, process listings, logs, screenshots or review JSON; use protected credential input supported by the environment.
Do not assume channel 1, omit `<Channel number>` or hard-code cipher 17 without negotiated Project support; record every queried channel.
Run only read operations. Do not invoke `user set`, `password`, `enable`, `disable`, `priv`, channel setaccess, payload enable or the broad internal Script without read-only review.
Do not clear security logs or truncate output; preserve complete per-channel raw-to-normalized traceability.
Distinguish unsupported channel, caller authorization failure, transport failure, empty slot and disabled user rather than reporting all as no accounts.
Stop on wrong target, unknown channel/column semantics, incomplete output, secret exposure or unexpected tool mutation; preserve evidence without a write workaround.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target/tool, channel set, field semantics, protected credentials, expected baseline and redaction.
Run complete read-only `user list <channel>` for every approved channel and collect raw output/status without truncation.
Normalize every slot/name/access flag/privilege/empty-disabled state and classify unsupported/auth/transport errors separately; optionally correlate read-only API/UI identities.
Confirm no account/channel audit change, archive redacted evidence and return facts without DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve channel discovery/set, column/privilege semantics, baseline and redaction.
Approve any internal Script revision only after proving read-only scope; otherwise use direct source command.
Review the complete per-channel matrix and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The `user list` verb fits, but it omits the source-required channel, assumes one channel, uses credential-exposing `-P` and fixed cipher 17, and lacks complete field/error interpretation. The unreviewed internal path may contain add/set writes and is not a safe substitute.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use protected `ipmitool ... user list <approved channel>` separately for every relevant channel with negotiated connection settings; never append account/channel mutations.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The exact IPMI list purpose, mandatory Channel number placeholder, referenced Script, display Criteria, no Bundle and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Discover/approve the channel set, collect complete protected per-channel user lists and normalize all slot/access/privilege states with explicit error handling and no writes.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC IPMI user and channel implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, IPMI spec/vendor extension level and ipmitool version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor IPMI channel/user-slot mapping, Project account baseline and IPMI access policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds channel completeness, secure credential handling, normalization, redaction and no-write audit while retaining `ipmitool user list`.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One channel does not prove all Project channels; optional API/UI correlation does not replace IPMI; listing does not prove Add/Delete behavior.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Channel set, schema, protected credentials, baseline and redaction.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Usernames/privileges are sensitive; channels can expose different slot/access views; ambiguous privilege labels need vendor mapping.

project_override_considerations: A read-only vendor API may be a Project override only when the original IPMI method, actual method, reason, engineer approval, per-channel/field equivalence and uncovered ipmitool coverage are recorded. The internal Script is not automatically approved merely because it is referenced.
expected_evidence: BMC/firmware/ipmitool identity, protected access method, supported/discovered channel set and field/privilege semantics
Complete raw redacted `user list <channel>` output and status for each relevant channel
Normalized channel/slot/name/access/privilege/empty-disabled matrix with explicit unsupported/auth/transport interpretations
Optional documented UI/API identity cross-check and expected-baseline differences
No account/channel write or secret exposure, preserved audit evidence and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define read-only IPMI user-list display. DeepSeek's missing channel and the broad Script path are method defects/coverage risks, not competing Master purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The list purpose and source command are explicit. Project/vendor inputs can define channels and schema, so the case is automatable after readiness inputs rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains FULLY AUTOMATABLE but materially corrects its channel-less, one-channel, credential-exposing command and adds complete normalization/error/no-write evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its classification and strengthens the boundary around the referenced broad Script and negotiated cipher/credential handling.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic full output with source-compliant per-channel inventory and auditability.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps Add/Delete IPMI writes entirely separate and prohibits their execution during View.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents incomplete one-channel results and accidental account writes while making the read-only IPMI inventory safely automatable and semantically auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: IPMI user tables are channel-scoped: the same slot can have different access flags/privilege by channel, and omitting the channel violates the source command. Complete evidence therefore needs a declared channel set and full per-channel matrix. Because the referenced script name includes add/set, direct read-only commands are safer until that exact revision is reviewed.
